units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Okay, I'm on a bridge. Here's my bet.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: This is just a bridge.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Let me make you lose. You're standing on the DuSable Bridge, the Michigan Avenue bridge.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It opened in 1920, after construction began in April 1918.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: A bridge that took two years.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And a plan that took much longer.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: A grand boulevard linking the south and north parks was proposed as early as 1891, and Daniel Burnham's 1909 plan for Chicago laid it out.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: There he is.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: There he is. Now look at the bridge itself.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's a bascule bridge, which means the road lifts up like a drawbridge.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And it has two decks.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Wait, two? I'm only on one.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The upper deck was for faster, non-commercial traffic.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The lower deck was for slower commercial traffic serving the docks and industries beside the river.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's believed to be the first double-deck bridge with a roadway on both levels.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: So there's a lower road under me.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Yes. Now look at the four stone houses at the corners.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Those are the bridgehouses, and in 1928 they were given sculptures.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The north ones show Joliet, Marquette, La Salle and Tonti, early explorers, and John Kinzie, an early settler.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And the person who paid for that work was William Wrigley Junior.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Not the gum Wrigley.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The gum man. Wrigley commissioned the sculptor James Earle Fraser.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The south ones were paid for by a monument fund.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: One of them shows the 1812 battle at Fort Dearborn, and the other, called Regeneration, shows Chicago rebuilding after the 1871 fire.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Fort Dearborn. I know that name.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The fort was built in 1803, and the south half of this bridge passes over its site.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Look at the sidewalk on the south side.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: There are brass markers that outline the old blockhouse.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: That's hidden in the pavement?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Hidden in plain sight, yes. And on the north side, near the Pioneer Court plaza, a plaque marks the homesite of Jean Baptiste Point du Sable.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: The name of the bridge.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: In October 2010 the bridge was renamed for him.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: He was a fur trader of African descent who married into the Potawatomi people, and he built a homestead and trading post near the river's mouth in the 1780s.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: He's often called Chicago's first permanent resident.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: So the bridge you were going to call just a bridge...

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Has a boulevard plan, a double deck, a fort, and a founder.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Fine. You win. It's not just a bridge.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: One more. In the southwest bridgehouse there's a small museum about the river and the bridge.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's called the McCormick Bridgehouse and Chicago River Museum, and it opened in 2006.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: In spring and fall, when the bridge is lifted for boats, you can see the gears work.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: In December, check the hours first.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: So here's where the lunch walk ends.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: For lunch, cross the bridge, turn left on Kinzie Street, and right onto Wabash Avenue.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The pizza place is inside the River Plaza building.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Pause the walk, and the next piece is the evening.
